title: Student identity linked to submission data
description: The student's identity (via login credentials and student ID) can be linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp), creating a persistent association between the student and their academic work.
assumptions: The system stores and processes both identity and submission data in a way that allows correlation.

title: Assignment submission data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App may expose student submission data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) to unauthorized users or systems, violating confidentiality requirements.
assumptions: The system has inadequate access controls or data protection measures for submission data.

title: Unauthorized submission usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially submit assignments on behalf of a student by exploiting authentication weaknesses, leading to false attribution of academic work.
assumptions: The authentication mechanism has vulnerabilities or the system lacks proper verification of student identity during submission.

title: Transmission of Student Identifiers to Grading Service
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the Assignment & Grading Service (P2). This creates an identifier threat as the data contains unique references to student identity that are being shared across system boundaries.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted in clear or insufficiently protected form during the P1→P2 flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation [1] I.2.1.1 applies to identifier threats; uncertainty on exact node mapping for Process→Process flows.

title: Processing of Identified Student Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes identified data including student id, course, and file reference. This constitutes processing of identified data as defined in threat tree node I.1.1.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading purposes without additional anonymization or pseudonymization.
uncertainty_note: Citation [3] I.1.1 applies to processing of identified data; uncertainty on whether this is the most specific node for this context.

title: Non-repudiation of Grading Actions
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) processes grading requests and submissions, creating evidence that could prevent individuals from denying their involvement in grading decisions or submission actions. This non-repudiation threat arises from the collection and processing of evidence linking individuals to specific actions.
assumptions: The system logs and retains evidence of who submitted what and who graded what, creating binding attribution.
uncertainty_note: Citation [4] describes non-repudiation as a privacy threat; exact tree node Nr.1.1 is inferred based on context.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure of Student Personal Information
description: The Assignment & Grading Service explicitly stores student ID, course, and submission time in the Assignment Store. This represents an intentional disclosure of personal data by design. The threat concerns whether this data collection is minimal and strictly necessary for the grading function, or if it exceeds what's required for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Student ID is considered personal/identifiable information under privacy regulations

title: Student Identifiability Through Stored Assignment Data
description: The stored assignment data includes student ID, which directly identifies the student. This creates a risk that the assignment submission data can be used to identify and profile individual students, potentially beyond the intended grading purpose.
assumptions: Student ID is a direct identifier that can be used to link assignment data to specific individuals

title: Processing of identifiable student submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes student submission data that contains personally identifiable information. When teachers request the queue of submissions, they access data that could identify individual students, including names, course assignments, and potentially other sensitive information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student submission data
description: Student submission data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly implemented. Teachers may access submissions beyond their authorized scope, or data could be leaked through improper logging, debugging, or API exposure.

title: Teacher account impersonation during login
description: The login process for teachers may be vulnerable to credential theft, phishing, or session hijacking attacks, allowing unauthorized actors to impersonate teachers and access the submission queue with elevated privileges.

title: Linkability of submissions to students and courses
description: The system may reveal patterns that allow linking submissions to specific students, courses, or teachers. This could expose sensitive information about student performance, course assignments, and teacher-student relationships through metadata or access patterns.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades and feedback
description: Teacher (EE3) may inadvertently or maliciously disclose student grades and written feedback to unauthorized parties (e.g., other students, parents, or external entities) through the Grades Portal Web App (P1).
assumptions: Teacher has access to the system and may share data outside intended recipients.

title: Identification of students through grade records
description: Student IDs and associated grades/feedback in the flow could be used to identify specific students, potentially exposing their academic performance to unauthorized observers.
assumptions: Student IDs are not properly anonymized or protected in the system.

title: Linkability of student data across systems
description: Grades and feedback data could be linked with other student information (e.g., attendance, behavior records) to create comprehensive profiles of students.
assumptions: Data may be shared or accessible across multiple systems.

title: Teacher impersonation and unauthorized grade recording
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher (EE3) to record false grades or feedback for students, compromising data integrity and student records.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be insufficient to verify teacher identity.

title: Lack of non-repudiation for grade submissions
description: Teachers may deny having submitted certain grades or feedback, making it difficult to establish accountability for recorded data.
assumptions: System may not maintain tamper-proof audit logs of all submissions.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records containing student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp could be accessed by unauthorized parties during the write operation or through compromised systems.
assumptions: Access controls on the grading service and database are not properly implemented or are bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for Process→DataStore flows.

title: Student Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain student id and grader id, enabling identification of specific students and their academic performance, which is sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Student id is a unique identifier that can be linked to individual students.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identification threat node.

title: Grade Record Tampering
description: Grades, feedback, or grader id could be altered during the write operation or after storage, compromising data integrity and academic records.
assumptions: The grading service or database lacks adequate integrity controls and audit mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a representative data degradation threat node.

title: Grader Identity Impersonation
description: The grader id field could be forged or impersonated, allowing unauthorized individuals to appear as legitimate graders in the system.
assumptions: Grader authentication and authorization mechanisms are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a representative usurpation threat node.

title: Linkability of Grade Records with Other Data
description: Grade records containing student id, course, and timestamp could be linked with other student data (e.g., enrollment records, demographic data) to create comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: Other data stores containing student information exist and are accessible.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability threat node; assumes external data exists for linking.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Student Data
description: Storage of student grade records may violate privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent, retention policies, or access controls are not implemented.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulations require specific handling of student academic records.
uncertainty_note: Using Nc.1.1 as a representative non-compliance threat node; assumes jurisdiction-specific regulations apply.

title: Processing of identified student grade data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified personal data (student grades and feedback) that can be linked to the specific student EE1. This processing of identified data creates privacy risks as the system handles sensitive academic information.
assumptions: The system has access to student-identifiable grade records
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 from context [5] applies to processing of identified data

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: Student grades and feedback may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, logging vulnerabilities, or data exfiltration. Even though the student is requesting their own grades, the system must ensure only authorized access.
assumptions: The system has access controls that may be bypassed or misconfigured
uncertainty_note: Standard threat for any system handling personal data

title: Linkability of student identity to grades
description: The student's identity can be linked to their grades and feedback data, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of academic performance over time. This linkability creates privacy concerns if the data is shared or analyzed.
assumptions: The system maintains records linking student identity to grade data
uncertainty_note: Standard linkability concern for any system processing personal data

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: Student grades and teacher feedback are sensitive personal data. If the portal lacks proper authentication/authorization controls, unauthorized users could access this data through the P1->EE1 flow.
assumptions: Portal has insufficient access controls; student grades are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations.

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Student grades displayed to EE1 could be linked with other data about the student (e.g., identity, other courses, behavioral data), creating a comprehensive profile that could be misused.
assumptions: Student data may exist in multiple systems that could be correlated.

title: Student Identity Usurpation
description: If authentication mechanisms are weak, an attacker could impersonate a student and access another student's grades and feedback through the P1->EE1 flow.
assumptions: Portal authentication may have vulnerabilities; student grades are tied to specific student identities.

title: Parent account impersonation during login
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent during the login process, potentially gaining unauthorized access to child's grades data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism is vulnerable to credential theft or social engineering
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for authentication impersonation threats

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's grades
description: Child's grades data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient or if the parent account is compromised.
assumptions: Access control mechanisms may have vulnerabilities or misconfigurations
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data disclosure threats

title: Child's identity linked through grades data
description: Grades data could be used to identify the child, especially if combined with other publicly available information.
assumptions: Grades data contains identifying information or can be correlated with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability threats

title: Parent-child relationship linkage
description: The system could link parent and child accounts, potentially revealing the parent-child relationship to unauthorized observers through data patterns.
assumptions: System logs or data structures may expose relationship information
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linkability threats

title: Unauthorized Access to Child's Grades Data
description: The grades portal web app (P1) transmits sensitive child academic information to the parent (EE2). If authentication or authorization controls are weak, unauthorized parties could intercept or access this data during transmission or storage.
assumptions: The system relies on standard authentication mechanisms that may be vulnerable to credential theft or session hijacking.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node for Process->ExternalEntity flows.

title: Child Identifiability from Grades Data
description: The grades, feedback, and submission history displayed to the parent could potentially identify the child, especially if combined with other publicly available information or if the data is shared beyond the intended parent.
assumptions: Grades data contains unique identifiers or patterns that could link to the specific child.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identifiability threat node.

title: Linkability of Child's Academic Data
description: The parent receiving grades data could potentially link this information to other data sources about the child, creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the intended scope of the grades portal.
assumptions: The parent has access to other data sources about the child that could be correlated with the grades information.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability threat node.

title: Parent Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the parent (EE2) to access the child's grades data through the portal, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft, phishing, or session hijacking attacks.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a representative usurpation threat node.

title: Excessive Data Sharing with Parent
description: The portal may share more data with the parent than necessary for legitimate parental oversight, including detailed submission history and feedback that could reveal sensitive information about the child's learning process.
assumptions: The system does not implement data minimization principles when determining what information to share with parents.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a representative data minimization threat node.

title: Identifiability of Personal Information in Account Management
description: Administrator creates/modifies accounts containing names, emails, and parent-child relationships that directly identify individuals. This personal data is processed and stored in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Administrator has access to create and modify account data containing personally identifiable information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account records to external parties
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory. If the directory is accessible to unauthorized parties, sensitive student and family information could be disclosed.
assumptions: The account directory has access controls that may not be properly enforced; external parties may gain access to the directory.

title: Unauthorized modification of account records and parent-child links
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory. Malicious actors could alter these records, potentially changing student information or family relationships, leading to incorrect grading or identity issues.
assumptions: The account directory lacks adequate integrity controls; authentication mechanisms may be bypassed.

title: Identification of students and family members through account records
description: Account records containing parent-child relationship links could be used to identify individual students and their family connections. This information may be sensitive and require additional protection.
assumptions: The account records contain personally identifiable information; the directory may be accessible to authorized personnel who could misuse this information.

title: Linkability of account records across different systems
description: Account records written by the grading service could be linked with data from other systems (e.g., enrollment, financial aid), creating a comprehensive profile of students and their families that may exceed privacy expectations.
assumptions: Other systems may share similar identifiers; data integration may occur across organizational boundaries.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5 as part of nightly backup and replication. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: Cloud provider EE5 has access to all transferred data including PII
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 chosen based on context [5] describing data disclosure as transfer to third party

title: Linkability of Personal Data Across Systems
description: Grade records and account directory data transferred to EE5 could be linked with other datasets (e.g., student IDs, timestamps) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.
assumptions: EE5 may retain data and potentially correlate with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Identifiability of Individuals Through Transferred Data
description: Account directory and grade records contain personally identifiable information that can directly identify students/users. Full data transfer increases identifiability risk.
assumptions: Account directory includes names, IDs, or other identifiers
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Unauthorized Access to Transferred Data
description: Data transferred to EE5 may be accessible by unauthorized personnel within the cloud provider organization or through security breaches.
assumptions: EE5 has internal access controls that may not be sufficient
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN methodology for Process→ExternalEntity flows

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Students/Parents/Teachers
description: Grade records in DS2 can be linked to specific students, parents, and teachers through the data flow to P2, potentially enabling correlation of multiple data points to identify individuals across different contexts.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiers that can be correlated with other data sources

title: Identification of Students from Grade Records
description: Grade records in DS2 contain student identifiers that could be used to identify specific students, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Grade records contain personally identifiable information

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Records
description: Grade records flowing from DS2 to P2 could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are not properly implemented, exposing sensitive student academic information.
assumptions: Access controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized access

title: Usurpation of Student/Parent/Teacher Identity
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) could be accessed by unauthorized users impersonating students, parents, or teachers to view grade records they should not have access to.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not be robust enough to prevent identity impersonation
